Paragraph: "As the one unable to see that lady but able to see beautiful trees the Love-god in me gains intensity...
Situation/Problem_Faced: The stark contrast between seeing beautiful nature and not seeing Seetha heightens Rama's inner desire and pain.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Rama analyzes the psychological mechanic of his grief—visualizing nature amplifies his desire for his absent wife.
Outcome/Resolution: He gains self-awareness about why his pain is escalating.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Aatma-Prabhava (Intensity of love arising from within the self)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The absence of the beloved combined with external beauty causes love (Aatma-Prabhava) to expand inside the soul, seeking union.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Cognitive awareness of triggers: recognizing that environmental beauty without the key attached person causes acute emotional escalation.
